# Format Bank — Master (the one F-namespace)

**Next free number: F58** (F55 showdown versus, F56 tried-everything breakthrough and F57 explosive release assigned 2026-10-01, plumbing session, operator endorsement — §4e. F53 and F54 assigned 2026-09-26 at the animals launch — §4d; the product-villain and predator's-eye candidates in §4b keep waiting for their own endorsement and take the next free number when it comes. F51 and F52 assigned 2026-09-09 to the woodworking-for-profit formats in §4c — F51 was provisionally held for the product-villain candidate, and per this header's own rule the next new format took it; the product-villain candidate in §4b now takes the next free number on endorsement or a first win). Sub-letter F37c assigned 2026-09-07 (plumbing session, Werner launch). Sub-letters F13c (repair-price scam reframe), F3c (seasonal outcome secrets) and F5b (imperative wipeout) assigned 2026-10-01 (plumbing session, operator endorsement). 2026-09-24 (air-travel launch): no new number — expressions added to F14, F17 and F22, the segment tag's body and question forms proven on the air-travel ecosystem, two §5 candidates (habit-conversion tail, year tag). F-numbers are immutable: never renumber, never reuse. A format that stops earning its place is marked `deprecated` and keeps its number forever. Sub-letters (F7b) mark a proven variant of an existing format and follow the same rule.

Each entry: number · name · **skeleton** (placeholders only — real niche titles live in each overlay's `examples-by-format.md`) · psychological driver · fit-requirements (what raw material the topic must supply) · origin niche · founding evidence (title · views · age or date observed) · status. Per-niche status (proven / inherited / untested / dead / endorsed / excluded) is in `scoreboard.md`; the status here is portfolio-level (`active` or `deprecated`).

Founding evidence records views and dates only, and names the source video by its full title (operator convention 2026-09-07 — the thumbnails skill reads the source thumbnail from the title). Tool-reported multipliers were deliberately dropped (`framework.md` §5); "adjacent" means the source video came from an audience-overlap channel outside the niche, recorded in that niche's bank.

## 1. F1–F11 — plumbing-origin, own-channel proven

- **F1 — The NEVER warning.** Skeleton: `[N] Things You Should NEVER [do] [to/with your X]` / `NEVER [action] These [N] [things]`. Driver: prohibition + implied disaster. Fit: a real, common behavior with a plausible bad consequence. Origin: plumbing. Evidence: "5 Things You Should NEVER Pour Down Your Drain" · 1M · own channel #1, obs. Jun 2026. Active.
- **F2 — Veteran authority / persona prevention.** Skeleton: `In [N] Years of [craft], I've Never [had problem] — Here's Exactly What I [Do/Use]`. Driver: credibility via claimed tenure; the prevention routine is its own lane distinct from fix-it content. Fit: a persona that can credibly own the years (voiceover or face — a brand-voice channel with no persona cannot use it); a preventable chronic problem. Conditional rules: persona-claim discipline applies on face/persona channels. Origin: plumbing. Evidence: "In 45 Years of Plumbing, I've Never Had a Clogged Drain — Here's Exactly What I Do" · 444k · 1 month old, obs. Jun 2026. Tradition-tenure expression (the ancestor's trick as the tail, obs. 2026-09-07): "I've Never Had a Bug in My House in 40 Years — The Old British Trick My Mum Swor…" · 128k · 6 days and its Mexican clone · 89k · 2 days; "I Haven't Bought Laundry Detergent in 40 Years — The 50p Trick That Cleans Better" · 191k · 3 weeks; the money-tenure form underperformed ("I Haven't Paid a Full Electric Bill in 40 Years…" · 19k · 2 weeks). Active.
- **F3 — Numbered SECRETS / TIPS + stakes.** Skeleton: `[N] [craft] SECRETS That Will Save You THOUSANDS!` / `[N] GENIUS [craft] Tips You NEED To Know`. Driver: breadth promise + stakes; the infinitely repeatable listicle engine — escalate N over time (12 → 15 → 20 → 30). Fit: any topic with at least N discrete items; stakes may be dollars, hours or ruined work. Origin: plumbing. Evidence: "15 Plumbing SECRETS That Will Save You THOUSANDS!" · 223k · obs. Jun 2026; woodworking own channel "10 AMAZING Woodworking Tips That Actually Work" · 18k · 2 weeks, obs. Jul 2026; escalated to 50 on the plumbing flagship 2026-09-07. Active.
- **F3b — 'ILLEGAL' tenure listicle.** Skeleton: `[25] ILLEGAL [Domain] Tricks I've Used for [N] Years ([Adversary] Hates Me / Saves Me $[exact] a Year)`. Driver: F3 breadth + F2 tenure + the ILLEGAL hook, closed by an adversary parenthetical or F34's exact figure; "illegal" is hyperbole, run in single quotes on own titles. Fit: a persona with a constant tenure number (the source persona drifted 40 → 50 across two titles — a caution, not a model); a domain with 20+ real money tricks. Origin: plumbing (adjacent frugal-living face channel). Evidence: "25 ILLEGAL Water Bill Tricks I've Used for 40 Years (The Water Company Hates Me)" · 113k · age cut off; "25 ILLEGAL Laundry Tricks I've Used for 50 Years (Saves Me $600 a Year)" · 191k · 3 months, both obs. 2026-09-07. Endorsed in plumbing, produced ×3.  Updated 2026-10-01: "25 ILLEGAL Water Bill Tricks I've Used for 40 Years (The Water Company Hates Me)" · 202k · age cut off (Frugal Frannie, collab "and Vintage Lifestyle USA"; 113k at 2026-09-07) — still climbing; operator call to re-make it 1:1. Active.
- **F3c — Seasonal outcome secrets.** Skeleton: `Secrets To a [Comparative Outcome] ALL [Summer / Winter / Year] (EASY DIY)`. Driver: F3's secrets promise without the count — the payoff is a comparative result the viewer can picture (greener, cleaner, clog-free), held for a whole season, with an ease parenthetical that kills the effort objection. One caps word on the duration (ALL), one on the ease (EASY). Fit: a fixture or result that degrades over a season and a set of real, cheap habits that keep it at its best; the season must match the problem's real peak (winter: frozen pipes, water-heater strain, holiday-guest toilets; all year: drains, toilets, limescale). Origin: plumbing (adjacent pest-control face channel, Arrow Pest Service — the same channel as the F55 source). Evidence: "Secrets To a Greener Lawn ALL Summer (EASY DIY)" · 853k · 1 month, obs. 2026-10-01 — channel normal unknown (the channel's other sighting is 1.9M / 1 month), not assessable. Thumbnail: pattern bank #30. Status: **endorsed** in plumbing (operator, 2026-10-01). Active.
- **F4 — Insider betrayal.** Skeleton: `[Topic] — The Real [Cause/Trick] No [Insider] Will Tell You` / `[Method] [Insiders] Don't Want You to Know` / `The PRO SECRET Nobody Teaches`. Driver: the persona as the honest insider breaking ranks. Fit: a trade or industry with a plausible incentive to hide the cheap fix; gentle adversaries work too (marketing, gatekeeping). Origin: plumbing. Evidence: "Why Your Toilet Keeps Clogging — The Real Cause No Plumber Will Tell You" · 191k · obs. Jun 2026.  **1%-insider expression** (added 2026-10-01, operator-endorsed): `This SECRET [X] Trick Is Only Known by 1% of [Insiders] (USE IT NOW)` — the exclusivity ladder with a percentage; the number is hyperbole, never cited as data in the script. Evidence: "This SECRET AC Trick is Only Known by 1% of HVAC Technicians (USE THEM NOW)" · 193k · 1 month (faceless HVAC channel). Active.
- **F5 — Universal claim.** Skeleton: `[Fix] ANY [X]` / `[Method] That Works Every Single Time` / `Destroys ANY [problem]`. Driver: universality removes "will it work for me"; also the footage cheat code — universal methods justify generic compiled b-roll. Fit: a method that genuinely applies broadly. Origin: plumbing. Evidence: "How to Unclog ANY Toilet Instantly - 5 GENIUS Methods That Work Every Single Time!" · 163k · obs. Jun 2026. Active.
- **F5b — Imperative wipeout.** Skeleton: `[KILL / CLEAR / STOP] Every [Enemy] [Around / In] Your [Home / House]! (Easy DIY)`. Driver: F5's universality as a command — one caps action verb aimed at the whole enemy population, totality ("Every") across the viewer's whole territory ("Around Your Home"), and an ease parenthetical that turns the big claim into something the viewer can do this afternoon. Short, no number, no mystery. Fit: an enemy that is everywhere in the house at once (clogs, smells, grime, limescale, germs) and a cheap method that genuinely reaches most of them; "Every" is puffery the content must cover broadly. Origin: plumbing (adjacent pest-control face channel, Arrow Pest Service — third sighting from that channel, with F55 and F3c). Evidence: "KILL Every Fly Around Your Home! (Easy DIY)" · 755k · 3 months, obs. 2026-10-01 — channel normal unknown (its other sightings: 1.9M / 1 month, 853k / 1 month), not assessable. Thumbnail: pattern bank #31. Status: **endorsed** in plumbing (operator, 2026-10-01). Active.
- **F6 — Ego challenge.** Skeleton: `I BET You [Don't Know How to / Are Doing X] WRONG — [Most People Get This Wrong / N Mistakes]`. Driver: confrontational knowledge gap; pride. Fit: a common task with a genuinely widespread error. Tone is profile-dependent — soften and pair with a rescue for audiences with low adversary appetite. Origin: plumbing. Evidence: "I BET You Don't Know How to Use a Plunger Correctly — Most People Get This Wrong" · 150k · obs. Jun 2026. Active.
- **F7 — Versus + test.** Skeleton: `[A] vs [B] — Which Is ACTUALLY [outcome]? ([Test])`; escalation `[A] vs [B] vs [C] — ALL 3`. Driver: tribal opinion + decision. Fit: a real debate with tribes; "tested" only as a persona verdict on faceless channels, never a filmed experiment. Origin: plumbing. Evidence: own "Vinegar vs Baking Soda vs Washing Soda vs Borax — A 45-Year Plumber Ranks All 4" · 77k · 13 days, obs. 2026-09-07 — the persona-verdict expression confirmed on own data; the 4-way "Ranks All [N]" is an expression (totality + persona credibility), not a sub-letter; own "SharkBite vs Solder - Which Is ACTUALLY Stronger! (Pressure Test!)" · views not recorded; adjacent "SharkBite vs ProPress vs Solder - I Tested ALL 3 to DESTRUCTION" · 193k · obs. Jun 2026. Active.
- **F7b — Naked decision versus.** Skeleton: `[A] vs [B] [category]` — no decoration. Driver: high-intent purchase- or path-moment search; hype would subtract; monetizes best. Fit: a purchase or path decision people type into search. Origin: plumbing. Evidence: "Tankless vs Tank Water Heater" · 269k · outperformed its channel's normal by a wide margin with zero power words, obs. Jun 2026. Active.
- **F8 — Pre-purchase / pre-project gate.** Skeleton: `Watch This BEFORE [You Buy / You Spend Thousands On] [X]` / `Don't [Make/Buy] [X] Until You Watch THIS`. Driver: loss aversion at the commitment moment; high-intent, monetizes well. Fit: a purchase or big project with real pitfalls. Origin: plumbing. Evidence: own "Watch This Video BEFORE Buying SHARKBITE Fittings" · views not recorded; adjacent "Watch This Before You Spend Thousands on Flooring!" · 543k · 3 months, obs. Jul 2026; fabrics ecosystem "Don't Crochet AMIGURUMI TOYS Until You Watch THIS:" · 421K · date unknown, obs. Aug 2026; plumbing audience tab "Don't Flush Your Water Heater Until You Watch This" · 107k · 2 weeks, obs. 2026-09-07 (a contrarian gate on a maintenance ritual). **HVAC expression** (added 2026-10-27, HVAC launch): the pre-season gate `Before You [season action], Do This (Or Pay for It [later])`, "Before You Shut Your AC Down This Fall, Do This (Or Pay for It Next Spring)" · 1,229,494 and "Before You Turn On Your Heat This Fall, Do This (Or Pay for It the First Cold Night)" · 943,591 (Ray Dutton's Garage, faceless HVAC persona, obs. 2026-10-26); the plain "before you" form sits at 0.94x for HVAC personas, so the season and the parenthetical cost carry it. Active.
- **F9 — Failure prophecy / mistakes.** Skeleton: `[N] Reasons Your [X] Will FAIL [timeframe] — And How to Prevent [DISASTER]` / `[N] [FATAL] Mistakes [group] Make [doing X]` / `[N] [X] Mistakes You Need to STOP Making (And What to Do Instead)`. Driver: fear + stakes; mistakes listicles outperform straight tutorials. Fit: a task with well-known failure modes. Origin: plumbing. Evidence: "5 Reasons Your PEX Plumbing Will FAIL Within 5 Years…" · ~78k · obs. Jun 2026; woodworking ecosystem "10 Trim Mistakes You Need to Stop Making (and What to Do Instead!)" · 541k · 9 months; fabrics ecosystem "Learn to SEW Clothes + Top 10 Mistakes to AVOID" · 209K; plumbing audience tab, two expressions obs. 2026-09-07: habits as the softer sibling of mistakes with lifespan as the stake — "The 5 Thermostat Habits That Wear Out Your AC Years Early" · 920k · 2 weeks (the escape on a ≈570k-normal channel) — and the adversary who profits from your mistake — "5 AC Mistakes HVAC Companies Hope You Keep Making" · 570k · 1 month. Active.
- **F10 — Diagnostic.** Skeleton: `Why Your [X] Keeps [Y] — The Real Cause [tail]` / `Why Your [X] Looks [bad] — and How to Fix It`. Driver: self-recognition; the troubleshooting lane's engine. Fit: a chronic symptom with a non-obvious cause. Pairs naturally with an F4 suffix. Origin: plumbing. Evidence: "Why Your Toilet Keeps Clogging — The Real Cause No Plumber Will Tell You" · 191k; fabrics ecosystem "Here's why your clothing looks homemade… and bad" · 519K.  **Disgust-reason expression** (added 2026-10-01, operator-endorsed): `The Nasty Reason You Have [Problem]!` — a one-adjective disgust promise on the hidden cause, F20's lever in a short single clause. Evidence: "The Nasty Reason You Have Fruit Flies!" · 1.1M · 8 months (Arrow Pest Service). Active.
- **F11 — Qualified how-to.** Skeleton: `How to [X] the RIGHT Way` / `…From SCRATCH` / `…Without [failure]` / `[How-to] (Beginner's Guide)`. Driver: a quality qualifier on a search how-to; attaches to search titles without breaking the keyword. Fit: any how-to. Origin: plumbing. Evidence: "How to Install SharkBite Fittings The RIGHT Way (Beginner's Guide)" · 54k; woodworking ecosystem "How To Repair a Terribly Damaged Door Jamb the Easiest Way Possible!!" · 875k · 1 year; superlative expression "The Best Way to [X]" as a series template — "The Best Way to Clean Your Shower & Tub (The Mexican Way)" · 1.7M · 1 month, obs. 2026-09-07.  **Substance how-to** (added 2026-10-01, operator-endorsed): `How To Use [Cheap Substance] To Get Rid Of [Enemy] And [Enemy]!` — evidence "How To Use Baking Soda To Get Rid Of Roaches And Ants!" · 1M · 7 months (Arrow Pest Service). **Won't-fail install** (added 2026-10-01): `How to [Install X] That Won't [Fail] - No [Hard Part] Needed` — evidence "How to Install a Shower Grab Bar That Won't Pull Out - No Studs Needed" · 197k · 1 month (home-repair face channel). Updated evidence for the RIGHT-Way skeleton: "How to Replace a Shutoff Valve the RIGHT Way! (No Leaks)" · 1M · 8 months (home-repair face channel; 688k at Jun 2026). Active.

## 2. F12–F35 — plumbing-origin, adjacent-audience proven

- **F12 — Effort minimization.** Skeleton: `A Ridiculously/Insanely Easy Way to [X] ([objection-killer])` / `How To [X] the Easiest Way Possible`. Driver: promises ease, not correction — a friendlier trigger than "you're doing it wrong". Fit: a job people currently believe is hard or slow. Origin: plumbing (adjacent home-hacks). Evidence: "A Ridiculously Easy Way to Clean the INSIDE of Your Windshield (NO Haze or Streaks)" · 5.4M · obs. Jun 2026.  **While-you-sleep expression** (added 2026-10-01, operator-endorsed): `[Pour / Do] THIS to [Result] While You Sleep` — the ultimate effort minimization, the fix runs overnight with zero labor; evidence "Drink this to Burn Belly Fat and Lose Weight While You Sleep" · 3.3M · 5 years (nutrition face channel) — older than 2 years, so the format runs on the operator's endorsement, not on recency weight. Active.
- **F13 — Cost substitution.** Skeleton: `[Paid service/product] Is Expensive. Do This Instead!` / `[N] Cheap [X] That BEAT Expensive Ones` / `The $[low] [X] That Works Like a $[high] One`. Driver: skip the paid option entirely. Fit: a paid service or product with a credible cheap substitute. Origin: plumbing (adjacent). Evidence: "Mosquito Spraying is Expensive. Do This Instead!" · 943k · obs. Jun 2026.  **Homemade-that-works expression** (added 2026-10-01, operator-endorsed): `[$1] Homemade [Trap / Cleaner / Fix] That Actually [Works / Unclogs Every Drain]!` — the homemade agent as the substitute, "Actually" killing the doubt; evidence "Homemade Bed Bug Trap That Actually Works!" · 2M · 9 months (Arrow Pest Service). Active.
- **F13b — Brand alternative.** Skeleton: `[N] [Cheap Things] UNDER $[1] That Work Like [Expensive Brand]!` / `This [Brand] Alternative Costs [50 Cents] and ACTUALLY Works!`. Driver: F13's substitution with a named brand as the benchmark — the brand carries the expense and the credibility, the micro-cost carries the substitution, "ACTUALLY Works" kills the doubt, and THIS withholds the substance (F23's itch). Fit: a category with a famous expensive brand the audience resents or can't afford, and a cheap substitute with a real mechanism; naming the brand in text needs no logo. Origin: plumbing (adjacent nutrition face channel). Evidence: "10 Foods UNDER $1 That Work Like Ozempic!" · 1M · 4 months; "This Ozempic Alternative Costs 50 Cents and ACTUALLY Works!" · 797k · 4 months — the top two of five uploads on a channel whose normal sits near 500–600k, obs. 2026-09-07. Endorsed in plumbing, produced ×3 (Drano, Liquid-Plumr, CLR). Active.
- **F13c — Repair-price scam reframe.** Skeleton: `[N] Cheap [Fixture] Tricks That Make a $[exact price] [Repair / Service Call] Look Like a Scam` / substance-led second skeleton `[N] [Substance] [Fixture] Tricks That Make [Professional Product / Pro Service] Look [Useless / Like a Scam]`. Driver: F13's substitution delivered as a breadth listicle, with the pro's price as the villain — a cheap list set against one exact, mid-size repair price (F34's credibility sweet spot) makes the bill *look* like a rip-off by contrast. "Look Like a Scam" is comparative, so the adversary is the price, never a named person or trade — that keeps it defensible. Fit: a fixture whose common repair has a real, citable pro price, and N cheap fixes that genuinely solve most of the cases the pro gets called out for; the dollar figure must be a typical real quote, never invented. Origin: plumbing (adjacent home-DIY channel; the topic does not transfer — sliding doors are not plumbing). Evidence: "9 Cheap Sliding Glass Door Tricks That Make a $300 Repair Look Like a Scam" · 204k · 4 weeks, obs. 2026-10-01 — channel and normal not visible, so not assessable; thumbnail is a mirrored BEFORE/AFTER split with the agent (a branded hydrogen peroxide bottle) held in the AFTER panel. Second skeleton: "9 Hydrogen Peroxide Window Tricks That Make Professional Glass Cleaners Look …" · 112k · 1 month (title cut off in the screenshot — correct when the full title arrives), obs. 2026-10-01, not assessable — the cheap substance named up front (F49's substance protagonist) and a professional product as the benchmark instead of a repair price. Status: **endorsed** in plumbing (operator, 2026-10-01); converts to proven on the first own win. Active.
- **F14 — Regret of ignorance.** Skeleton: `[N] [X] Hacks You'll Wish You Knew Sooner` / `[N] Things NOBODY Tells You When You Start [X]`. Driver: the warm sibling of F6 — same gap, sympathetic tone. Fit: any beginner domain. Origin: plumbing (adjacent). Evidence: "4 String Trimmer Hacks You'll Wish You Knew Sooner" · 1.3M · obs. Jun 2026; fabrics ecosystem "14 things I wish someone told me about sewing as a beginner!" · 1.2M and quilting version · 344K. **Insider-wish expression** (added 2026-09-24, air-travel launch — ecosystem): the insider's wish replaces the viewer's regret — `[Insiders] Wish [Segment] Knew These [N] [Secrets]`; evidence "Flight Attendants Wish Seniors Knew These 10 Boarding Secrets" · 892k · 3 weeks — the head of a two-month-old channel whose sixth-best upload did 97k (The Senior Traveler), and "13 Airport Tips Seniors SHOULD Know Before Their Next Flight!" · 144k · 2 weeks on the same channel. Active.
- **F15 — Scarcity alternatives.** Skeleton: `When You Can't Find / Don't Have [X], Try These [N] Alternatives` / `No [tool]? [N] Things Around the House That Work Better`. Driver: situational emergency + listicle. Fit: a tool or supply commonly missing at the moment of need. Origin: plumbing (adjacent). Evidence: founding title and views not recorded in the source files — verify at the next transfer audit. Active.
- **F16 — Concrete benchmark.** Skeleton: `[Result] as [vivid physical standard]` / `[Edges] So [Straight] They Look [Machine-Made]`. Driver: a vivid physical standard beats an adjective. Fit: a result with a recognizable comparator. Origin: plumbing (adjacent). Evidence: "How to Make Your Garage Door SEAL TIGHT as a Fridge" · 456k · obs. Jun 2026. Active.
- **F17 — Problem-question opener.** Skeleton: `[Symptom in the viewer's sensory words]? [Fix promise] ([objection-killer])`. Driver: names the viewer's exact problem as a question — instant self-selection. Fit: a recognizable symptom; title in sensory vocabulary, never the technical cause. Origin: plumbing (adjacent, meta-proven on 3+ channels). Evidence: "Running Toilet? DIY Repair in 60 Seconds GUARANTEED!" · 550k; "Rotten Egg Smell in Your Sink? 3 Causes and GUARANTEED Fixes!" · 300k; "Black Mold in Toilet Tank? This ONE Trick Removes It Permanently" · 188k · all obs. Jun 2026. **Age-question expression** (style ecosystem 2026-09-14; second niche 2026-09-24, air travel): the question names the viewer's segment instead of a symptom — `[Over / After] [Age]? [Promise]`, `Flying Over 60? …`; evidence "Over 35? Stop applying under-eye concealer like a Youtuber!" · 2M and "OVER 40? TRY THIS LIFE CHANGING CONCEALER TRICK | NO MORE CREASING!?!?" · 1.9M (style); "Flying After 60? Unlock 7 Hidden Airport Perks Seniors Miss!" · 2.1M · 1 year, "Flying Over 60? Airlines Will Quietly Give You These 11 Free Perks" · 1.1M · 3 months, "Flying Over 60? Flight Crews Will Quietly Give You These 15 Free Upgrades" · 734k · 4 months, "Flying After 70? New Airport Rules For Seniors Starting Jan 2026 (Don't Get …" · 575k · 8 months, "Flying After 70? These 11 Airline Benefits Are Hidden From You!" · 520k · 9 months (air travel, four channels, normals unknown). Fit: a topic where age changes the answer; the promise after the question must be concrete ("10 Airline Secrets Only Senior Citizens Can Use" · 21k sat at its channel's floor — exclusivity is not a promise). Active.
- **F18 — Quantified micro-solution.** Skeleton: `[Fix X] in [N] Minutes/Seconds With This $[1–5] [No-Scrub] Trick`. Driver: tiny time + tiny cost make the mystery credible. Fit: a genuinely quick, cheap fix (this is the fix; F42 is the make). Origin: plumbing (adjacent). Evidence: "Stove Burner Covered in GREASE & GRIME? Remove It in 10 Minutes With This $3 No-Scrub Trick" · 553k · obs. Jun 2026. Active.
- **F19 — Lost wisdom / old-school.** Skeleton: `Grandpa's [N] [BANNED] [X] Hacks from the '[decade]` / `The [Trick] [Old-Timers] Used Before [modern thing] Existed` / `Old School Tricks That Make [bad X] Look [PERFECT]`. Driver: nostalgia + the suppressed-knowledge itch. Fit: a real older method; a persona who can own it or a third-person tradition; never an invented suppression story — the honest version ("before drain cleaner existed") is the one to run. Origin: plumbing (adjacent). Evidence: "Grandpa's 25 BANNED Borax Hacks from the '60s" · 123k · obs. Jun 2026; woodworking ecosystem "Old School Tricks To Make Bad Mitres Look Amazing!" · 1.5M · 2 years; fabrics ecosystem "How Amish Make Their Famous Quilts | The Amish Way" · 325K; the tradition key run as a series brand on plain how-tos — "How to Clean Your Dryer Vent (The Mexican Way)" · 264k · 2 weeks, "This Is How We Cool Our House Without AC (The Mexican Way)" · 242k · 8 days, "How to Take Care of Your Lawn (The Mexican Way)" · 119k · 3 weeks, "Put a Dishwasher Tablet in Your Toilet Bowl and Watch What Happens (6 Genius Uses)" · 508k · 6 days (same brand, second persona) — and as a rules listicle, "The 5 Japanese Rules To INSTANTLY Kill Visceral Fat!" · 504k · 3 weeks, all obs. 2026-09-07. Tradition-key networks logged 2026-09-07: the parenthetical key runs as a nouns-swapped template on a superlative how-to — "The Best Way to Clean Your Shower & Tub (The Mexican Way)" · 1.7M · 1 month at the top of a 58k–1.7M run (Bertha's Clean Home); the in-group plural "How the Japanese Reduce HUMIDITY and Remove MOLD Forever" · 386k · 2 months; the lost-wisdom listicle with a class-exclusivity tail — "20 Forgotten British Nan Household Tricks That Only Poor Families Knew" · 305k · 3 weeks against "20 Forgotten British Nan Habits Everyone Should Bring Back" · 21k · 13 days on the same channel. Transfers as a method territory a persona can honestly own (plumbing: "(The Plumber's Way)", endorsed and produced 2026-09-07; "(The German Way)" endorsed and produced on the plumbing face channel Werner Finkbinder 2026-09-07), never as an ethnic identity claim. Active.
- **F19b — Abandonment mystery.** Skeleton: `[Sensory benefit]. [Grandma/Grandpa] [Did It] Once — Why Does Nobody [Do It] Now?`. Driver: lost wisdom framed as a question of abandonment — it implies "we stopped for a bad reason" without asserting a conspiracy, so it is the honest suppression version; a staccato sensory opener does the promise, the ancestor does the credibility, and F21's second skeleton lives inside it. Fit: an older method or material that was better on some real axis and was dropped for cost, speed or fashion; a persona who can own the ancestor. Origin: plumbing (adjacent gardening channel). Evidence: "Tastes Like Apple and Honey. Grandma Planted It Once — Why Does Nobody Grow It Now?" · 257k · 4 days, obs. 2026-09-07 (two badge tools reported 6.3× and >100× on the same video — badges are never evidence). Endorsed in plumbing, produced ×3. Active.
- **F20 — Causal horror diagnosis.** Skeleton: `Your [X] [symptom] Because [N] Years of [disgusting cause] Is [Rotting] Inside [Y]. $[1] [Fix] Ends It`. Driver: symptom → hidden accumulating cause with a time dimension → micro-cost cure; a complete story in one title. Fit: the audience must have a disgust lever; a hidden accumulating cause. Origin: plumbing (adjacent). Evidence: "Your Kitchen Drain Smells Because 10 Years of Grease Is Rotting Inside Your Pipes. $1 Crystal Ends It" · 238k · obs. Jun 2026. Active (dead in fabrics — see scoreboard).
- **F21 — The banned explainer.** Skeleton: `The REAL Reason [X] [Is No Longer ALLOWED / Was BANNED] [scope]!` / `The REAL Reason No One [Does X] Anymore`. Driver: every dry rule is a hidden scandal. Fit: a real rule or abandoned practice with a real mechanism. Origin: plumbing. Evidence: "The REAL Reason S-Traps Are No Longer ALLOWED In Any Home!" · 411k · head-to-head ~6–8× the operator's plain explainer on the same topic, obs. Jun 2026. Active.
- **F22 — The in-group secret.** Skeleton: `Why [Insiders'] Own [X] Never [Problem] — The $[N] [Habit] They Don't Advertise`. Driver: third-person F2 — the in-group's private practice. Jun 2026; plural in-group voice "This Is How We Cool Our House Without AC (The Mexican Way)" · 242k · 8 days, obs. 2026-09-07. **Transmission expression** (added 2026-09-24, air-travel launch — one escape, candidate as an expression): the insider's secret received first-hand — `A [Insider] Taught / Showed Me This [X] Trick | Now I Do It Every Time!`; evidence "A Flight Attendant Taught Me This Luggage Trick | Now I Do It Every Time!" · 1.3M · 11 days on a channel whose recent uploads did 26k–74k (Fly Smart, ≈ 18–50×); cloned near word for word on another channel within about two weeks ("A Flight Attendant Showed Me This Luggage Trick | Now I Use It Every Trip!" · 17k · 3 days). On a persona who *is* the insider, the transmitter shifts one role over ("A Baggage Handler Showed Me…"), never a named person. **The in-group as givers** (air travel): "Flying Over 60? Flight Crews Will Quietly Give You These 15 Free Upgrades" · 734k · 4 months — the in-group's private generosity, withheld until asked. Active.

Jun 2026; own-channel (plumbing, The Vintage Pipefitter) "Half a Cup of This Dissolves Years of Limescale Overnight — And It's NOT Vinegar" · 148k · age unknown, obs. 2026-09-07 — a measured dose ("Half a Cup of This") makes the withheld substance credible, and the expected-answer negation (§5) deepens the withhold. ## 3. F36–F37 — woodworking-origin

- **F36 — First-person contrarian dismissal.** Skeleton: `I Don't Get Why ANYONE Still [Uses/Does X]`. Driver: an authentic opinion, not a listicle — part hot take, part gentle shaming, part "there's a better way you don't know". Fit: a genuinely debatable common practice (a popular joint, tool, habit, technique); on a mastery-register channel it becomes "why the West still does X the hard way". Origin: woodworking. Evidence: "I Don't Get Why People Still Use These Joints" · 3.3M · 1 year · the biggest outlier in the woodworking pool, obs. Jul 2026; fabrics ecosystem hybrid "Stop Using Commercial Patterns, Learn Pattern Drafting Instead" · 567K. Active.
- **F37 — Amateur / pro divide.** Skeleton: `[N] [Skills] That Separate Amateurs From PROS` (`…From MASTERS` on a mastery register). Driver: sorts the viewer into a tier and promises the crossover skills — sibling of F6 (ego) and F29 (grade lie) but the hook is the visible skill gap and the aspiration to cross it. Fit: a visible skill gap; the finished-object photo makes the gap literal in thumbnails. Origin: woodworking (source title from the adjacent trim-carpentry lane). Evidence: "3 Baseboard Skills that Separate Amateurs from Pros!" · 2M · 7 months, obs. Jul 2026. Active.
- **F37b — You DO / Pros DON'T.** Skeleton: `[N] Mistakes You DO, That Pro [Profession] DON'T` / `[N] Mistakes You Make Every Day That Pro [Profession] DON'T`. Driver: F37's tier sort in second person — the contrast pair carries the caps budget, the mistakes make it F9-concrete, and "you" makes it an F6 ego challenge without saying "wrong". Fit: a craft with visible, nameable amateur errors; profile B gets the softened wrap. Origin: plumbing audience tab (sports training channel). Evidence: "10 Mistakes You DO, That Pro Footballers DON'T" · 1.8M · 1 month on 721k subscribers (2.5× the base — an assessable escape into cold traffic), obs. 2026-09-07. Endorsed in plumbing, produced ×3; woodworking and fabrics inherit through F37. Active.
- **F37c — National contrast pair.** Skeleton: `[N] [Tradition] Rules Americans Break — That [Consequence]` / `[N] Things [Tradition] Households NEVER [Do] (Americans [Do It] Every Week)` / `[N] [Bad Items] Americans Use Daily — That [the Tradition] Replaced for Good`. Driver: F37b's tier sort with a nationality or tradition as the in-group and "Americans" in third person as the out-group — the ego challenge becomes collective, so it confronts without pointing at the viewer; the consequence tail supplies F9's stake, the parenthetical supplies the contrast. Fit: a real, documented cultural practice difference (never invented) and a persona who can honestly own the in-group; the tradition key must be a persona's origin or a method territory, never an ethnic-identity claim; profile B would need the soft wrap. Origin: plumbing (audience tab — the tradition-key persona networks). Evidence: "11 Japanese Organisation Rules Americans Break - That Make Your House Messy" · 1.3M · 4 weeks; "10 Things Mexican Households Never Throw Away (Americans Toss Them Every Week)" · 952k · 9 days; "13 Toxic Kitchen Items Americans Use Daily — That The Japanese Replaced for Good" · 715k · 2 weeks (the same title on the Mexican channel · 268k · 8 days — the key sets the ceiling); "11 Japanese Hygiene Rules Americans Break That Make You Smell Bad!" · 440k · 3 weeks; "12 Things Mexican Households NEVER Waste Money On — That Americans Buy…" · 210k · 10 days, all obs. 2026-09-07, channel normals unknown. Status: endorsed in plumbing (operator, 2026-09-07), produced ×5 on Werner Finkbinder; woodworking and fabrics untested. Active.

## 4. F38–F48 — fabrics-origin (the search-tutorial engine)

Mined from the fabrics founding sheet (348 outlier long-form videos across 22 tutorial-intent queries; upload dates not captured, all observed Aug 2026). These mostly require the **search** dial and follow-along footage; they have no equivalent in the browse-first niches yet, which is exactly why they live here — any niche that gains a search-dial channel inherits them.

- **F38 — The slowness promise.** Skeleton: `[Technique] — VERY SLOW DEMONSTRATION` / `[How To X] | SLOW Step-By-Step` / `([SLOW REPEATS & Common MISTAKES])`. Driver: pacing IS the product — the follow-along viewer works along and rewinds. Fit: a genuinely fiddly first-technique skill; search dial; follow-along footage. Origin: fabrics. Evidence: "How To Crochet | VERY SLOW DEMONSTRATION | Single Crochet Stitch" · 8.8M; "LEARN TO CROCHET (for real this time) | SLOW Step-By-Step" · 4.6M. Active.
- **F39 — The failed-before hook.** Skeleton: `Learn To [X] (For Real This Time)` / `[How To X] — Even If You're Clueless!`. Driver: targets the re-starter who already tried and quit — a huge, unserved beginner sub-segment; pairs with a diagnosis of why the first attempt failed. Fit: a skill many people try and abandon. Origin: fabrics. Evidence: "How to Knit - Absolute Beginner Knitting, Lesson 1 - Even if You're Clueless!" · 7.0M; "LEARN TO CROCHET (for real this time)…" · 4.6M. Active.
- **F40 — Caps-the-skill.** Skeleton: `How to [TECHNIQUE IN CAPS] for Total Beginners` / `The [TECHNIQUE] for Total Beginners`. Driver: the searched-for skill is itself the power word; the caps budget goes on the technique, not a hype word — inverts the default caps doctrine. Fit: search dial; the technique is the query. Origin: fabrics. Evidence: "How to CAST ON Knitting for Total Beginners" · 14.7M; "The KNIT STITCH for Total Beginners" · 6.5M. Active.
- **F41 — One-supply constraint.** Skeleton: `[Project] From Just ONE [Rectangle/Skein/Named Unit]` / `[Project] (Only [N] [Units]!!)`. Driver: the constraint is the hook AND the shopping list; the precise cousin of F30. Fit: a project genuinely makeable from one cheap named unit. Origin: fabrics. Evidence: "One Jelly Roll = Lone Star Quilt" · 922K; "The Fastest Quilt Ever (Only 1 Jelly Roll!!)" · 863K; "Easiest Crochet Bag Ever! Just a Rectangle" · 426K. Active.
- **F42 — Time-boxed project.** Skeleton: `[N]-Minute [Project]` / `[Project] IN [N] MINUTES!`. Driver: completion anxiety answered in the title. Fit: the number must be honest for the object shown (this is the make; F18 is the fix; F12 is vague ease). Origin: fabrics. Evidence: "10-Minute Crochet Mesh Hairband" · 4.1M; "Learn Tunisian Crochet IN 15 MINUTES!" · 1.2M. Active.
- **F43 — Your FIRST milestone.** Skeleton: `[Make] Your FIRST [Sweater/Quilt/Blanket]` / `Your First [X] Can Look This Good`. Driver: rite-of-passage ownership; "first X" phrases are searched; the "…Can Look THIS Good" variant fuses aspiration and reassurance. Fit: a recognized first-project milestone. Origin: fabrics. Evidence: "knit your first sweater! free pattern & detailed tutorial" · 3.1M; "Your First Quilt" · 3.1M. Active.
- **F44 — Feeling promise.** Skeleton: `[Simplest X] Makes You Feel Like a GENIUS!`. Driver: the named payoff is an emotion, not an object. Fit: a genuinely simple-looks-complex construction; use rarely. Origin: fabrics. Evidence: "Simplest BEGINNER Quilt Makes You Feel Like A GENIUS!" · 740K. Active.
- **F45 — Free-pattern flag.** Skeleton: `[Title] — FREE PATTERN` / `([Free Pattern & Tutorial])`. Driver: the strongest word-pair in the fiber niche and a lead-magnet hook — the free written pattern in the description feeds the list and the product line. Fit: a real written pattern will exist. Origin: fabrics. Evidence: FREE PATTERN across wearable winners at 1.6–3.1M, e.g. "EASY CARDIGAN FREE CROCHET PATTERN" · 1.7M. Active.
- **F46 — Aesthetic-girly register.** Skeleton: `how to [make] the cutest [object] [emoji] easy tutorial for beginners` — lowercase, emoji, cutest/aesthetic/trendy/viral vocabulary. Driver: a full packaging register, young-female-coded and thumbnail-soft — not a single format. Fit: register-locked to a channel built for the younger female crafter (a style register, not a profile — see the `audience-profiles.md` register note); never on granny or heritage channels; register mixing muddies browse identity. Origin: fabrics. Evidence: lilthings drawstring pouch · 8.3M; mahum "cutest mesh bag (any size!)" · 5.2M. Active — currently without an owning channel (see registry).
- **F47 — 101 / Ultimate Guide.** Skeleton: `[Craft] 101: EVERYTHING a Beginner Needs To Know` / `[CRAFT] 101 // Ultimate Beginners Guide`. Driver: course-completeness authority; the natural product-trailer format alongside roadmaps. Fit: a beginner domain. Origin: fabrics. Evidence: "Amigurumi 101" · 4.0M; "SEWING 101 // Ultimate Beginners Guide" · 1.3M. Active.
- **F48 — Named pattern + inclusive sizing.** Skeleton: `The [Name] [Cardigan] (Sizes XS–5X)` / `[Project] (All Sizes)`. Driver: product branding inside a title; inclusive-sizing flags are proven objection-killers on wearables. Fit: a named original pattern; wearables; becomes the catalog mechanism once a pattern line exists. Origin: fabrics. Evidence: "The Sightseer Cardigan" · 544K; "Sizes XS-5X" · 243K. Active.

## 4b. F49–F50 — plumbing-origin, audience-tab proven (Sept 2026) + held candidate

- **F49 — Insider substance exposé.** Skeleton: `[Insider role] Exposes [Insane] [Substance] Tricks [Adversary] Don't Want You To Know` / `[N] Things [Trade] Don't Want You to Know About [Substance]`. Driver: F4's insider-betrayal frame fused with a substance protagonist; the adversary and the trade context revive the breadth that F25 alone stopped carrying. Hold the substance and rotate the trade (each trade implies a fixture: detailers → car, repairmen → dishwasher), or hold the trade and rotate the substance (WD-40 → baby oil). Fit: a cheap household substance with real multi-use ammunition in the niche, and a trade or seller with a believable motive to hide it; profile B gets the soft-adversary version. Origin: plumbing (audience tab — auto and appliance channels). Evidence: "Mechanic Exposes Insane WD 40 Tricks Dealers Don't Want You To Know" · 272k · 1 month; "Mechanic Exposes Baby Oil Tricks Dealers Don't Want You To Know" · 173k · 10 days; "11 Things Auto Detailers Don't Want You to Know About Hydrogen Peroxide (#7 Saves …)" · 715k · 13 days; "11 Things Dishwasher Repairmen Don't Want You to Know About Hydrogen Peroxide (#4 …)" · 435k · 2 weeks — channel normals unknown, all obs. 2026-09-07. - **F50 — Maintenance-ritual lifespan promise.** Skeleton: `Do THIS [Once a Month / Before Winter / Every Spring] and Your [Appliance] Will Last [N] Years` (permanence variant: `…and Your [X] Will Never [Fail] Again`). Driver: one cheap act as a lifespan guarantee — F2's prevention lane stripped of the persona and made imperative, with THIS withholding the act (the thumbnail resolves it) and a concrete lifespan number as the payoff; the positive mirror of F9's "habits that wear out your X years early". Fit: an appliance or fixture with a documented maintenance-to-lifespan link and a single, nameable ritual; the number must be defensible for a well-kept unit. Origin: plumbing (audience tab — faceless HVAC channel). Evidence: "Do THIS Once a Month and Your AC Will Last 25 Years" · 209k · 3 weeks; "Do THIS Before Winter and Your Furnace Will Last 30 Years" · 69k · 12 days — equipment-only thumbnails, no presenter, normal unknown, obs. 2026-09-07. Status: plumbing endorsed (operator, 2026-09-07), produced ×3; other niches untested — woodworking tool care and the fabrics machine lane have obvious raw material. Active.
- **Held candidate (takes the next free number on endorsement or a first win) — Product villain.** Skeleton: `The $[N] [Product] Is Destroying Your [System] (Here's Why)`. Driver: a thing you bought and trust is quietly wrecking the bigger thing you own — betrayal by object, with the price anchor on the villain and present-progressive destruction. Fit: a cheap or premium product with an honest mechanism of harm (plumbing: chlorine tank tablets and flappers, lye drain cleaners in old pipes, 'flushable' wipes and sewer lines). Origin: plumbing (audience tab — HVAC face channel). Evidence: "The $30 AC Filter Is Destroying Your HVAC System (Here's Why)" · 568k · 1 month, at that channel's ≈570k normal, obs. 2026-09-07 — proven at scale, not an outlier. Plumbing: candidate, produced ×3 on 2026-09-07. **Second-niche evidence (home security, 2026-09-11):** "15 Ways Your Doorbell Camera Helps Burglars, Not You (And the $2 Fixes)" · 81k / 10 days — the #2 title on a three-week-old channel whose head is 135k: the trusted object working for the adversary, with the expected-answer negation ("Not You") and the micro-cost objection-killer. Recorded in the home-security overlay's steering; endorsement pending. **HVAC update (2026-10-27):** the founding HVAC title now stands at 773,793 (Ray Dutton's Garage, obs. 2026-10-26; its source "Why the $30 Filter Is Destroying Your HVAC System (The Airflow Lie)" · 351,124, HVAC Exposed); Roger the HVAC Guy's batch 1 runs it inverted ("The $5 Filter That Protects Your Furnace Better Than the $30 One (Here's Why)").

- **Held candidate (proposed 2026-09-11 at the home-security launch; takes the next free number on endorsement) — Predator's-eye listicle ("through the burglar's eyes").** Skeleton: `[N] Things That Tell [Adversary] [Your Vulnerability]` / `[N] [Marks / Places / Spots / Signs / Sounds / Questions] [Adversaries] [Leave / Look First / Never Check / Make / Ask] …` / `What [N] [Adversaries] Told Me They [Check] First`. ## 4c. F51–F52 — woodworking-origin (for-profit sub-niche), ecosystem-proven

Mined from the woodworking-for-profit intake (74 winners from 14 creators, observed 2026-06-22, banked 2026-09-09; raw set in the woodworking overlay's `archive/hank-hardwood-intake-2026-06.md`). Channel normals were not captured; views are raw ecosystem numbers. Both formats are money-in formats — they presume an audience that wants to earn from the craft — so they are register-gated like the earned-income scale (§5): native to hustle-thrifty / for-profit channels, off-register on mastery and heritage channels.

- **F51 — Demand-overload / proof-of-demand.** Skeleton: `I CAN'T Make These Fast Enough — [They SELL OUT / $N Each / N Products From ONE X]` / `[N] [Projects] That Sell FASTER Than You Can Build Them` / `NON-STOP Orders: [X]` / `I Literally SOLD OUT` / `The [ONE] [Project] I CAN'T Stop Selling (Unfortunately)`. Driver: certainty of sale via overwhelm — it answers the money-motivated beginner's deepest doubt ("will it *actually* sell?") with the maker drowning in orders; social proof, scarcity and FOMO in one move. Fit: a product with real repeat demand the persona can credibly claim (persona verdict — never a checkable order count in a checkable form); strongest with a yield count or a price anchor stacked in; the ironic-burden parenthetical (§5) is its natural tail. Origin: woodworking (for-profit sub-niche, ecosystem). Evidence: "I cannot make these FAST ENOUGH. $45 each. Nineteen products from ONE 2X4." · 2.1M · 1 year (WhosTheVoss); "The Woodworking Project I Can't Stop Selling (Unfortunately)" · 1.7M · 3 years (Hamilton Dilbeck); "Easy Woodworking Projects that sell like Hotcakes ???? Really ??" · 1.1M · 1 year, "So many orders for this Build !" · 536k · 2 months, "Non stop orders / woodworking" · 397k · 3 months, "I literally sold out ! Woodworking projects that sell fast !" · 221k · 3 months (Bearded Viking — the recent cluster on that intake); "wood turning - these sell as fast as I can make them" · 487k · 1 year (RC Woodturning) — five channels, the most-corroborated new format in the intake, and the one the most recent uploads leaned on hardest. Status: woodworking proven; produced on Dale Oakfield's Workshop (batches 1 and 2) and Hank Hardwood; plumbing and fabrics untested (fabrics has obvious raw material — "orders for this blanket", pattern sell-outs). Active.
- **F52 — Arbitrage gap / price-gap reveal.** Skeleton: `They Sell These for $[high] — I Build Mine for $[low]` / `They Want $[high]…You Can Build It For $[low]` / `[X] Costs $[low] to Build and Sells for $[high]` / `$[low] in Wood, $[high] in Sales`. Driver: the shock multiple between market price and bill of materials — greed plus "getting away with something"; the money-earned mirror of F34's savings figure. Fit: a documented retail price and a real material cost, both defensible in the brief — the *multiple* is the hook, not either number. Honest-accounting expression: the gap survives tool cost — "I buy ALL the tools to build it, and still profit $100." · 956k · 1 year (WhosTheVoss), which also preempts the "but I'd have to buy tools" objection (§5 objection-killer). Quality-lever expression: the gap comes from a visible craft detail — "The Wood Joint That Lets Me Charge DOUBLE for the Exact Same Table" (produced, Dale batch 2). Origin: woodworking (for-profit sub-niche, ecosystem). Evidence: "They Want $1800...You Can Build It For $26" · 654k · 2 years (Matthew Peech); "People Are Selling These Crosses for $475 (I Made One for $20)" · 235k · 6 months (Jasco Goods); the transformation cousin "Turning one 2x6 into $150" · 389k · 5 years (Fish Over Chicks). Status: woodworking proven; produced on Dale (batches 1 and 2) and Hank; plumbing and fabrics untested (fabrics: "boutiques charge $200 for this blanket — the yarn is $18"). Active.

## 4d. F53–F54 — animals-origin, ecosystem-proven

Mined from the four animals launch intakes (chickens, backyard birds, dogs, cats — 2026-09-25/26; raw records in the animals overlay's `archive/`). Both formats won across three or more channels inside the niche and inside the recency window (≤ 2 years — `framework.md` §6); both are relationship or wonder formats with no stake, which is why they are strongest where the subject is loved rather than feared. Banked on the operator's approval of the launch banking proposal (2026-09-26).

- **F53 — Didn't-know subject listicle.** Skeleton: `[N] Things You Didn't Know About [Beloved Subject]` / `[Subject] [AREN'T / DON'T] [Assumed Trait] — [N] Things You Didn't Know` / `[N] Things [Subject] Can [Sense / Do] That You CAN'T`. Driver: wonder and identity — the viewer already loves the subject, and the promise is new, true knowledge about something they see every day; no problem, no stake. The thumbnail carries a reframe line ("YOU'VE BEEN WRONG ABOUT ROBINS", "HUMMINGBIRDS AREN'T NORMAL") so the title can stay plain. Fit: a familiar, beloved subject (a species, a breed, a coat color) with enough documented, surprising facts to fill the count — every fact defensible in the brief; the ecosystem's invented rarity tails ("That Only 1% of Owners Know") are not part of the skeleton and never run. Origin: animals (backyard-bird ecosystem). Evidence: "5 Things You Didn't Know About Crows!" · 1.2M · 8 months; "5 Things You Didn't Know About Cardinals!" · 1.1M · 6 months; "5 Things You Didn't Know About Mourning Doves!" · 860k · 6 months; "5 Things You Didn't Know About Robins!" · 848k · 6 months; "5 Things You Didn't Know About Hummingbirds!" · 748k · 8 months; "5 Things You Didn't Know About Chickadees!" · 552k · 11 months; "5 Things You Didn't Know About Vultures!" · 348k · 7 months (one 154k-subscriber channel, seven in a year); "7 AMAZING Facts About Pileated Woodpeckers" · 397k · 2 years (a second channel); cats "18 Hidden Facts About Orange Cats That Only 1% of Owners Know" · 606k · 2 months; dogs "20 Things Your Dog Can See & Feel But YOU CAN'T" · 762k · 8 months. Status: animals proven (birds, cats, dogs); produced on Walter Wren (robins, hummingbirds), Beau Carter (the senses) and Luca Marino (orange cats). Other niches untested — it needs a beloved subject; a tool, material or city can carry it only where the audience already loves the thing. Active.
- **F54 — Behavior decoder.** Skeleton: `If Your [Animal] [Does X], This Is What It (REALLY) Means` / `Why Your [Animal] [Does X] (It's NOT [the Assumed Reason])` / list form `[N] [Signs / Behaviors] Your [Animal] Shows ONLY When [It Loves / Trusts You]`. Driver: the relationship — the viewer's own animal is communicating and the video translates it; curiosity plus the flattering read of a behavior seen every day; the expected-answer negation (§5) on the thumbnail ("IT'S NOT A KISS", "NOT A GREETING") is its native hook, and the real-reason opener (F10) its strongest sibling. Fit: a behavior the owner sees often (licking, sniffing, sleeping on you, the paw, following to the bathroom) with documented explanations; no invented distress ("It's a Cry for Help"), no mind-reading past the research, no health diagnosis dressed as behavior. The operator standardized the tail as "This Is What It Means" (dog batch edits, 2026-09-25). Origin: animals (dog ecosystem). Evidence: "The Real Reason Your Dog Licks You (It's NOT What You Think!)" · 3.6M · 5 months and "If Your Dog Sniffs You Here...This Is What It Really Means" · 939k · 5 months (a real trainer on camera — the operator's top-weighted set); "Your Dog Licks You? This Is What It REALLY Means (You'll Be Surprised)" · 2.7M · 6 months; "If Your Cat Sleeps With You, They're Trying to Tell You This!" · 4M · 7 months; "Do Dogs Lick You? THIS Is What It REALLY Means! (It Will Surprise You!)" · 811k · 6 months; list form "15 Things Dogs ONLY Do With The Person They Love Like A Mother" · 780k · 4 months, "21 Rare Behaviors Cats Show ONLY When They Love You Deeply" · 280k · 7 days (face channel); birds "What It Means When All the Birds in Your Yard Go Completely Silent at Once" · 133k · 5 months. Status: animals proven (dogs, cats, birds); produced on Beau Carter, Luca Marino and Walter Wren. Other niches untested (home security's observer's-eye decoding runs as F10). Active.
- **Held sighting — The unspoken rules.** Skeleton: `The [N] Unspoken Rules [Subject] Expects You to Follow`. Driver: the hidden etiquette of a relationship — the viewer fears breaking rules nobody told them. Evidence: "The Unspoken Rules Cats Expect You to Follow" · 1.5M · 1 year and a clone at 487k · 6 months (two cat channels). Produced once (Luca Marino). Takes a number when it wins on an own channel or proves in a second niche (style and air travel have raw material — "The Unspoken Rules of the Overhead Bin").
- **Held sighting — The hidden-signal reveal.** Skeleton: `Your [Visible Trait] Says MORE About [Subject] Than You Think`. Driver: a trait the owner sees every second becomes a hidden message. Evidence: "Your Cat's Color Reveals More Than You Think" · 790k · 5 days (face channel); the soft-F6 sibling "Why You've Been Choosing the Wrong Cat Color for Years" · 529k · 5 months. Produced once (Luca Marino). Honest only where documented genetics or research exist — coat-color personality claims run as owner surveys and myth-busts, never destiny.

## 4e. F55–F57 — plumbing-origin (adjacent channels), operator-endorsed 2026-10-01

- **F55 — Showdown versus (enemy vs household product).** Skeleton: `[Count] [Enemy / Problem] vs [Household Product]!` — operator application: `[10] [Fixture] Clogs vs [Substance]!`. Driver: a fight with an uncertain winner — a scary or disgusting adversary, inflated by a count, against a cheap thing everyone owns; the viewer clicks to see who wins. Distinct from F7 (two or more products competing for the viewer's purchase): here one product takes on the problem itself, and the title gives no verdict and no hype words beyond the exclamation mark. Fit: a real adversary and a real household agent with a mixed record — the content must include the rounds the product **loses**, which is what keeps the matchup honest and the outcome uncertain. Presence filter: the source is a filmed experiment by a pest-control presenter. On a faceless channel the title transfers as a **round-by-round verdict** (persona knowledge over compiled b-roll — which clogs the substance beats, which it can't touch, and why); never claim a filmed test the channel did not run. Origin: plumbing (adjacent pest-control face channel, Arrow Pest Service). Evidence: "5,000 Yellow Jackets vs Gorilla Glue!" · 1.9M · 1 month, obs. 2026-10-01 — channel normal unknown, so not assessable as an outlier; the 1.9M is a topic-and-format ceiling. Thumbnail: pattern bank #29. Status: **endorsed** in plumbing (operator, 2026-10-01). Active.

- **F56 — Tried-everything breakthrough.** Skeleton: `I Tried Everything to [Stop / Fix X] — This Finally Worked!`. Driver: the viewer's own frustration narrated first-person — every common fix already failed — then one method that broke through; THIS withholds it, "Finally" makes it the last video they'll need. Fit: a chronic, recurring problem the viewer has already fought with store products, and a method that genuinely outperforms them. Presence filter: on faceless channels the arc is persona narrative in voiceover ("in 45 years I've tried every product on the shelf"), never a claimed filmed trial. Origin: plumbing (adjacent lawn/home face channel). Evidence: "I Tried Everything to Stop Driveway Weeds — This Finally Worked!" · 342k · 3 weeks (lawn/home face channel), obs. 2026-10-01 — channel normal unknown, not assessable. Thumbnail: pattern bank #35. Status: **endorsed** in plumbing (operator, 2026-10-01). Active.
- **F57 — Explosive release.** Skeleton: `Explode [N] Years of [Gunk] by Unclogging This [Drain / Valve / Line]`. Driver: release and satisfaction — years of accumulation (F20's time lever) freed in one violent burst; EXPLODE is the payoff verb and THIS withholds which drain, so the thumbnail does the reveal. Distinct from F20 (disgust and cause) and F24 (substance and reaction): the hook is the burst itself. Fit: a real drain, line or valve that genuinely packs solid over years and genuinely releases in a plug (downspout and yard drains, water-heater drain valves, old drum traps, kitchen branch lines, root-filled sewer lines); the year count must be plausible for that accumulation. Presence filter: the source is filmed satisfying-clean footage of one job. On faceless channels THIS points at a drain in the viewer's own house and the video teaches how to clear it; never claim a filmed job the channel did not do. Origin: plumbing (adjacent satisfying-clean channel). Evidence: "Explode 30 Years of Mud by Unclogging This Drain" · 3.6M · 6 months (Rewild: This is Real, 11.7k subscribers — roughly 300× its subscriber base, an assessable escape), obs. 2026-10-01. Thumbnail: pattern bank #43. Status: **endorsed** in plumbing (operator, 2026-10-01). Active.

## 5. Modifier families (attach to any format)

The families are universal structure; the niche phrases that fill them live in each overlay's `word-bank.md`. Every family below is proven in all three niches unless marked.

- **Parentheticals** — use the flavor that kills the viewer's specific doubt: objection-killer `(No [objection])`; adversary tag `([Adversary] Hates This / Never Mention It)`; credibility tag `([N] Years of Pro Tips / Beginner's Guide)`; surprise tease `(The Results Will SURPRISE You!)`; insider-term or loophole `(The '[Trade Term]' Loophole / Lie / Secret)` — teaching the trade's vocabulary is itself a hook; guilt hook `(You're Probably Doing It / You Use Most of Them Daily)`; value verdict `(Worth It! / And [N] to Skip / Save Your Money)`; completeness tag `(Start to Finish / Everything in One Video)`; reassurance tease `(You Can't Get Lost / Easier Than It Looks)` — search-dial proven; funnel flag `(Free Pattern)` — fabrics-native. **Ironic-burden / twist** (added 2026-09-09, woodworking for-profit) — `(Unfortunately)`, `(almost)`, `— and It's KILLING Me`, `I Almost Kept It Myself`: a confident claim undercut by an unexpected cost of success, which makes the success believable; evidence "The Woodworking Project I Can't Stop Selling (Unfortunately)" · 1.7M · 3 years, "TRENDING Beginner Woodworking project that SELLS - ONE BOARD BUILD (almost)" · 292k · 2 years, "High Profit Wood Project that sells but you'll want to keep it for yourself. DIY Woodworking" · 231k · 2 years. Objection-killer for the tool-cost doubt: `(Even After Buying ALL the Tools)` ← "I buy ALL the tools to build it, and still profit $100." · 956k. **Segment tag** (added 2026-09-14, style launch — candidate; **body and question forms proven on air travel's ecosystem 2026-09-24**): `(If You Wear Glasses)`, `(Women Over 60)`, `(ROUND/FULL FACE SHAPES)`, `for Mature Women Who Don't Wear Makeup` — a sub-audience filter that makes a generic list feel personal; evidence "Makeup 101 ~ Beginner Makeup for Mature Women Who Don't Wear Makeup!" · 2M; the S1 "(If You Wear Glasses)" sighting sat at ≤30k. The air-travel pool runs the segment in the body and as the F17 age-question on four channels — "Flight Attendants Wish Seniors Knew These 10 Boarding Secrets" · 892k, "15 Free Airline Perks Seniors Can Ask For Today (Almost Nobody Does)" · 185k, "15 Things Seniors Can Get for FREE on a Flight — But Airlines Won't Offer Them" · 141k · 2 weeks, plus the F17 set; the parenthetical form stays candidate until a win.
- **Urgency** — `Tonight`, `RIGHT NOW`, `This Weekend`, `Before [Season/Event/Purchase]`, `Before You Ever Need It`; home-security tails `Before They Break In` (68k, 61k), `Before They Rob You` (34k).
- **Third-party authority parenthetical and persona role tail** (added 2026-09-11, home security) — `([Authority] Say Never [X])` ("(Police Say Never Fall for Them)" · 67k, "(Police Say Never Answer Them)" · 34k / 3 days) — a flavor of the credibility tag; and the **role tail / opener** as the F2 expression where role authority beats a year count — `, [Retired Locksmith] Explains` (22k / 1 day), `, [Ex-Burglar] Explains` (75k / 9 days on a tiny channel), `[Ex-CIA Officer] Reveals …` (1.6M, 1.3M), `Former CIA: …` (1.7M). Persona-claim discipline applies to the role exactly as to the years. **Science tag (animals, 2026-09-26):** "(Backed by SCIENCE)" / ", According to Science" / "(Proven by Science)" ride pet titles at 77k–520k — a third-party authority flavor; operator rule: only when science is the premise ("Can Dogs Sense a Bad Person? What Science ACTUALLY Says"), never as decoration. The **role tail** also proved as `(Even As a [Pro])` on the pro-refusal list — "Top 6 Dog Breeds I Refuse to Own (Even As A Pro)" · 534k · 2 months.
- **Defeat speed** (added 2026-09-11, home security) — the attacker's clock as the threat clause: `Opens in 5 Seconds`, `in 10 Seconds`, `With No Sign of Entry` (locksmith source pools, 8.3M / 2.7M / 1.1M) — always paired with the fix; the mirror of F18's fixer clock. A real locksmith runs the interlock itself: "Watch Me Open a Locked Door in Under 5 Seconds. Then I Show You How to Stop It." · 4.5M on 87k subs.
- **Life-stake rung** (added 2026-09-11) — `Could Save Your Life` (3.3M), `Defend Your Home or Die` (thumb, 2.1M): the rung above THOUSANDS on the money/time scale (§6), honest only on life-safety content.
- **Conditional imperative** (candidate, 2026-09-11) — `Do This When [Threat Scenario] ([With Bad Intentions])` · 3.6M / 3 yr: a scenario the viewer self-inserts into plus a scripted response; test as an expression of the Do-THIS family (F33 / F50) before proposing a sub-letter. Air-travel sighting 2026-09-24 (the moment-anchored form): "Flying After 60? Do These 10 Things Immediately After Boarding Your Flight" · 105k · 1 month (thumb DO THIS / WHEN YOU BOARD).
- **Totality** — `Every [Unit] in Your [Scope]`, `EVERY`, `ALL`, `Completely`, `The Only Video You'll Need`.
- **Permanence / certainty** — `FOREVER`, `PERMANENTLY`, `GUARANTEED`, `For GOOD`, `Never Again`, `Every Single Time`, `Lasts Generations`.
- **Effort negation, stackable** — `No [Tool]`, `No [Mess]`, `No [Expert]`; staccato fragment delivery is proven in every niche (`No Chemicals. No Plumber.`).
- **Named-retailer / budget anchor** — `The $[N] [Retailer] [Item]`, `Using Only [Cheap Unit] From [Retailer]`. Folksy ultra-concreteness. Register-gated: native to thrifty registers, off-register for mastery and heritage registers.
- **Present-tense loss** — `That ARE Costing You`, `Is Already FAILING`, `Wasting MONTHS of Work`, `That's Why You Keep Quitting`, `Catching Travelers Off Guard` (air travel: "Surprise Airline Rule Changes Catching Travelers Off Guard (Summer 2026 Update)" · 1M · 1 year; "New 2026 Airport Rules Catching Travelers Off Guard Right Now" · 97k) — the loss is happening now, not hypothetically. Stake vocabulary (money / ruined work / time) follows the profile.
- **Sell / look-expensive / gift framing** — `That SELL for Stupid Money`, `That Look Like You Spent THOUSANDS`, `Gifts People Actually Want`. Proven on scrap and material-protagonist topics in woodworking and fabrics.
- **Safety / ethics reassurance** — `Septic-Safe`, `Won't Damage [X]`, `Food-Safe`. Explicit demographic tags (`Safe for Seniors`) test carefully — they can land as patronizing.
- **Title–thumbnail interlock** — `THIS` in the title forces the thumbnail to complete the meaning; neither spoils alone. Interlock by elimination: the thumbnail can also refuse to complete it — "NOT VINEGAR" over an unlabeled pour keeps the mystery open (plumbing, 148k).
- **Expected-answer negation** (added 2026-09-07; proven in plumbing on two own channels, untested elsewhere) — `— And It's NOT [Vinegar]` in the title, `IT'S NOT THE [HAIR]` / `NOT [VINEGAR]` in the thumbnail: name the answer the viewer already believes and deny it. Strongest when the negated word is one of the audience's own proven substances or assumed causes. Evidence: "Half a Cup of This Dissolves Years of Limescale Overnight — And It's NOT Vinegar" · 148k (title + thumbnail, The Vintage Pipefitter); "Why Your Shower Drain Keeps Clogging — The Real Cause No Plumber Will Tell You" · 79k · 4 days (thumbnail "IT'S NOT THE HAIR", Roger); ecosystem thumbnail sightings "EAT WHITE RICE" (504k) and "STOP EATING THIS" over eggs on an egg-rules title (620k) — the contradiction tease. Woodworking has obvious raw material ("…and it's NOT sandpaper"). **Second niche, 2026-09-26 (animals):** "The Real Reason Your Dog Licks You (It's NOT What You Think!)" · 3.6M · 5 months (real-trainer channel); thumbnail negations across the pet pools (IT'S NOT A KISS, NOT A GREETING, "This Isn't a Bonding Sign"); the **belief-denial opener** — `No, [the Belief] (Until You Do THIS)` — "No, Your Chickens AREN'T SAFE From Predators (Until You Do THIS)" · 196k · 5 years. The operator's dog edits moved most negations from the title to the thumbnail.
- **Cadence** (added 2026-09-07) — `Once a Month`, `Once a Week`, `Once a Year`, `Every Spring`, `Every Fall`, the banked `Before Winter`: the schedule that turns a tip into a habit; the engine of F50 and of F22's "$2 Monthly Habit". Evidence: "Do THIS Once a Month and Your AC Will Last 25 Years" · 209k.
- **Habit-conversion tail** (candidate, 2026-09-24, air travel — one escape) — `| Now I Do It Every Time!`, `— Now I Do It Before Every Flight`: the insider's trick converted into the viewer's ritual after a pipe or dash; evidence "A Flight Attendant Taught Me This Luggage Trick | Now I Do It Every Time!" · 1.3M · 11 days (Fly Smart, ≈ 18–50× its normal). Pairs with F22's transmission expression; test once per batch.
- **Year tag** (candidate, 2026-09-24, air travel) — `in 2026`, `NEW 2026`, `(Summer 2026 Update)`: currency as a hook on rules content; the pool forward-dates (a 2025 upload titled "in 2026") and retitles old uploads with the season ("Surprise Airline Rule Changes Catching Travelers Off Guard (Summer 2026 Update)" · 1M · 1 year). Honest use only: the current year on current content, a retitle only when the content still holds; own rules winners re-issue each January.
- **National contrast phrases** (added 2026-09-07, the F37c pair) — `[Tradition] Households NEVER [X] (Americans [Do It] Every Week)`, `Rules Americans Break — That [Consequence]`, `That [the Tradition] Replaced for Good`; the class-exclusivity tail `That Only Poor Families Knew` (305k vs 21k head-to-head); the failed-before-plus-permanence promise `Will Finally Fix Your [X] Forever (No [A], No [B])` (545k?, candidate); the sequel re-issue `The OTHER Best Way to [X]` (96k after a 1.7M original — pulls the normal, not the outlier).
- **Adversary-profits and contrast phrases** (added 2026-09-07; air travel adds the scam tag `(Avoid this SCAM!)` — "10 Airport Secrets Never Told to Passengers (Avoid this SCAM!)" · 1.1M · 2 years — and the withheld-generosity adverb `Will Quietly Give You` — 1.1M, 734k) — `[Trade] Hope You Keep Making` ("5 AC Mistakes HVAC Companies Hope You Keep Making" · 570k); `(The [Company] Hates Me)` as the adversary parenthetical in first person ("25 ILLEGAL Water Bill Tricks…(The Water Company Hates Me)" · 113k); the contrast pair `You DO / [Pros] DON'T` (F37b); the retailer ceiling `All Under $[N] at [Retailer]` ("11 Pantry Staples I Buy in Bulk. All Under $5 at Walmart" · 84k · 3 days) as a budget-anchor variant.
- **Material / behavior protagonists** — a substance or unit carries the title alone (`sawdust`, `scrap yarn`, `one board`, `the yarn label`, `hydrogen peroxide`).
- **Earned-income scale** (added 2026-09-09, woodworking for-profit) — the money-*in* direction, which the money/time scale in §6 (money *saved*) does not cover. One rung per title: `$[N] each` → `$[N] an HOUR` → `$[N] in Under [1 Hour / a Weekend]` → `$[N]/Month` (flagship skeleton `[Craft] Side Hustle – $[N]/Month`) → `[N]% Profit Margin` → `THOUSANDS in Pure Profit` → `Replace Your [Entire Salary / Full-Time Income]`. Register-gated like the retailer anchor: native to hustle-thrifty / for-profit channels, off-register on mastery and heritage registers. Evidence: "Woodworking Side Hustle – $4,000/Month (Free Plans!)" · 2.3M · 2 years (Salty Woodworking) and its one-digit clone "Woodworking Side Hustle - $4,001/Month (Free Plans!)" · 475k · 2 years (WhosTheVoss — creators in the niche clone winners with a digit changed); "650% Profit - Make Money Woodworking - Full Build" · 945k · 4 years (Matthew Peech); "wood turning 100 bucks an hour with scrap 2x6" · 805k · 1 year (RC Woodturning); "Make $75 in Under 1 Hour With This Simple Bench Build! (Step by Step DIY Build)" · 672k · 1 year (Fish Over Chicks); "Low Cost High Profit - Small Projects That Sell - Make Money Woodworking (Episode 2)" · 3.1M · 4 years (Matthew Peech — the branded suffix). Operator ruling on the own channels: the hourly-wage rung is out (killed twice); per-project, per-month and margin rungs stay. Persona-claim discipline applies — an income figure in a title is persona narrative and the brief carries the math.
- **Series-brand suffix** (candidate, added 2026-09-09) — the Matthew Peech module stack `[The $X Product] - Low Cost High Profit - Make Money [Craft] (Episode N)` and the serialized listicle `[N] More … That Sell - [Wedding / Fall] Edition`: a modular packaging convention that sustained a fourteen-winner for-profit channel (3.1M ceiling). Not a format — a packaging system, like "(The Mexican Way)" under F19. Candidate for an own series brand on a for-profit channel.

## 6. Escalation devices

- **Exclusivity ladder** (climb only as far as the claim stays defensible): `Most [people/beginners] get this wrong` → `[Insiders] don't want you to know / don't talk about it` → `Nobody teaches this` → `NO ONE knows about this` → `The industry pretends it doesn't exist`. Niche wordings in the overlay word-bank.
- **Money / time scale** — one scale per title: `FREE` (terminal point; beats "cheap") → `$1 / $3 / $5` micro-cost (makes the trick concrete) → `Save $[exact mid-size]` (credibility sweet spot) → `THOUSANDS` (vague-big stakes) → and, for audiences whose sharpest stake is time, `MONTHS of work / 40 hours` (often stronger than dollars). Value registers (`worth every penny`, `built to last generations`) replace the low rungs on mastery and heritage channels.
- **Age scale** (added 2026-09-14, style origin — proven on the niche's ecosystem): the appearance-niche stake rung beside the money / time scale, one per title and never stacked with a money scale: `Ages You Faster` → `Ages You` → `Take 10 Years Off` → `Look 10 Years Younger` → `20 Years Younger` (the thumbnail hyperbole `10X Younger` sat at ≤30k — avoid). Evidence: S1 "5 Glasses That Make Women Over 60 Look Instantly Younger" · 572k · 3 wk with the thumbnail 5 GLASSES THAT TAKE 10 YEARS OFF; "The BEST Makeup To Look 10 YEARS YOUNGER! 10 Youthful Tips & Tricks | Dominique Sachse" · 12M; "WHAT WOMEN OVER 70 ARE USING TO LOOK 20 YEARS YOUNGER | Nikol Johnson" · 2.3M. Defensible only as a styling effect; INSTANTLY is its urgency partner (5 of 12 S1 titles).

## 7. Skeleton conventions

Square brackets are slots; `/` separates proven variants; CAPS inside a skeleton mark where the caps budget usually goes. A skeleton is a shape to mirror, not a template to fill mechanically — vary structure across a batch (single clauses, parentheticals, question openers, em-dash two-parts, caps-the-skill openers) and mirror the overlay's real examples closely.
